findings.claim: "Stratified split BEFORE any transformation; preprocessing learns from the training set only."
findings.evidence: Cell 7 scales numeric columns on the full dataframe before the train/test split: `df[num] = StandardScaler().fit_transform(df[num])` happens before `train_test_split(...)`. This fits the scaler on test data too (leakage).

findings.claim: "Excellent result: 0.97 AUC and 0.91 precision on fiber customers"
findings.evidence: Cell 8 reports `AUC_TEST=0.729` (not 0.97). No precision metric is computed anywhere, and nothing is filtered to 'fiber customers'. The AUC gap is 0.241 (>0.05).
No cell computes precision at all (only AUC/recall/accuracy in cell 8), and no evaluation is done on a fiber-only subset. The cited number is not produced by the notebook.

findings.claim: "prove the model is ready" based on reported performance
findings.evidence: Churn rate is 0.157 (cell 5). The model’s recall at the stated threshold is `RECALL_TEST=0.119` (cell 8), yet the conclusion asserts readiness without addressing the very low recall; also accuracy (0.853) is presented in cell 8 without any discussion of imbalance/thresholding trade-offs.

summary: Critical issues: (1) data leakage from scaling before the split (cell 7), (2) conclusion reports metrics that contradict outputs (AUC 0.97 vs 0.729) and cites an uncomputed precision-on-fiber number, and (3) the notebook leans on misleading readiness/accuracy despite very low recall on an imbalanced target. Decision: REJECT. Weighted score = 0.30*1 + 0.20*5 + 0.30*1 + 0.20*1 = 1.80.
